pages.heading: The Skill Tree
pages.body:
Magical development is tracked across five skill trees. The registrant spends skill points to unlock nodes within them.

Nodes are permanent once unlocked. The witch or wizard in question is advised to plan their development with care, as the Ministry does not issue refunds and the Wizengamot has twice declined to compel one.

pages.heading: Proficiency
pages.body:
Proficiency measures the registrant's casting experience in a given spell or ability. It increases through repeated successful casting.

Proficiency follows an S-curve: early gains come quickly, while true mastery is slow to achieve. The proficiency pip row on the heads-up display indicates the registrant's current tier.

pages.heading: Proficiency Tiers
pages.body:
There are five tiers: Novice, Apprentice, Adept, Expert, and Master.

Each tier unlocks stronger spell variants or reduced casting costs. Numeric thresholds are not published. The Department finds that registrants informed of the exact figure tend to stop one cast short of it.
